body.statement: For every \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M_{n,K,d,0}\), there is a finite exact recovery policy using only targets of size at most \(d\). If \(d=0\), it outputs the empty oriented union without a paid query. If \(d\ge1\), the \(n\) singleton targets recover \(R_{\mathbf G}\) from \(t\in D_{\{a\}}(a)\). For each head \(t\), process its mixture ancestors with strict descendants before strict ancestors, maintain the already certified set \(P_t\subseteq\operatorname{pa}_{\cup}(t)\), and query \(I=P_t\cup\{a\}\) for the next candidate \(a\); declare \(a\in\operatorname{pa}_{\cup}(t)\) exactly when \(t\in D_I(a)\), and stop when \(|P_t|=d\). The policy outputs \(\mathsf T(\mathbf G)\) and uses at most \(n+n(n-1)\) paid queries.
body.justification: This verifies that the cycle-free endpoint uses the degree budget itself: certified parents block every indirect surviving path before the next source is tested.
body.gap: VariciKatzWeiSattigeriTajer2024Interventional gives the reverse-ancestor induction but does not formulate the resulting finite minimax recovery policy over the completed shared-kernel model class.
body.consumer: The feasibility theorem uses this policy to certify that panels of size \(d\), rather than \(d+1\), suffice whenever mixture ancestry is cycle free.
